symptoms: Olive-green or brown scab-like spots on leaves and fruit
Spots may coalesce and cover large areas
Infected leaves often curl and drop early
Fruit develops rough, corky, cracked lesions
Apple Scab.treatment: Apply a fungicide labeled for apple scab (e.g. captan or myclobutanil) every 7–10 days during wet spring weather. Remove and destroy fallen leaves to reduce overwintering spores. Prune to improve air circulation.

symptoms: Circular brown spots with purple margins on leaves (frog-eye leaf spot)
Fruit rots from the calyx end, turning black and mummified
Cankers with reddish-brown margins appear on branches
Apple with Black Rot.treatment: Prune out all dead and cankered wood at least 15 cm below visible infection. Apply captan or thiophanate-methyl fungicide from pink bud stage through petal fall. Remove mummified fruit from the tree and ground.

symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on the upper surface of leaves
Tube-like projections (aecia) on the underside of leaves
Infected fruit develops orange lesions and deforms
Cedar Apple Rust.treatment: Apply myclobutanil or propiconazole fungicide from pink bud through petal fall stage. Remove nearby eastern red cedar or juniper trees if possible (they are the alternate host). Plant rust-resistant apple varieties.

symptoms: No disease detected — your apple plant appears healthy!
Healthy Apple.treatment: Maintain regular watering, fertilizing, and annual pruning. Apply preventive fungicide spray each spring as a precaution.

symptoms: No disease detected — your blueberry plant appears healthy!
Healthy Blueberry Plant.treatment: Maintain soil pH between 4.5–5.5. Mulch around plants to retain moisture. Prune out old canes each year to encourage new growth.

symptoms: White powdery coating on young leaves and shoots
Affected leaves curl upward and may become distorted
New growth is stunted and spindly
Cherry with Powdery Mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur-based or potassium bicarbonate fungicide at first sign of infection. Improve air circulation by pruning dense canopy. Avoid overhead watering. Remove infected shoots.

symptoms: No disease detected — your cherry plant appears healthy!
Healthy Cherry Plant.treatment: Ensure good drainage and avoid overhead irrigation. Apply dormant copper spray in late fall to prevent fungal diseases next season.

symptoms: Tan to gray rectangular lesions parallel to leaf veins
Lesions initially appear water-soaked and turn grayish-tan
Severe infection causes leaf blighting and premature death
Corn (Maize) with Cercospora and Gray Le.treatment: Apply strobilurin-based fungicide (e.g. azoxystrobin) at tasseling stage if disease pressure is high. Plant resistant hybrids. Rotate crops and till in crop residue to reduce overwintering inoculum.

symptoms: Small, circular to elongated brick-red pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture and release powdery reddish-brown spores
Severe infections cause leaves to yellow and die
Corn (Maize) with Common Rust.treatment: Apply propiconazole or trifloxystrobin fungicide if rust is detected early (before tasseling). Plant rust-resistant hybrids for next season. Monitor fields weekly during cool, humid weather.

symptoms: Long (2.5–15 cm), elliptical, gray-green to tan lesions on leaves
Lesions may have wavy, irregular margins
Severely blighted leaves dry out and die, reducing photosynthesis
Corn (Maize) with Northern Leaf Blight.treatment: Apply propiconazole, azoxystrobin, or pyraclostrobin fungicide. Plant resistant hybrids. Rotate fields away from corn for at least one season. Incorporate or till residue to reduce spore load.

symptoms: No disease detected — your corn plant appears healthy!
Healthy Corn (Maize) Plant.treatment: Ensure adequate nitrogen fertilization. Scout fields weekly for early disease signs. Rotate crops annually.

symptoms: Small, circular tan spots with dark brown borders on leaves
Fruit shrivels into hard, black, mummified berries
Infected tendrils and canes develop dark, elongated lesions
Grape with Black Rot.treatment: Apply mancozeb, myclobutanil, or captan fungicide from bud break through 4–6 weeks after bloom. Remove and destroy all mummified berries and infected canes. Improve canopy airflow with proper training and pruning.

symptoms: Interveinal striping and discoloration (tiger-stripe pattern) on leaves
Fruit shows dark brown spotting and shriveling
Internal wood may have brown streaking (esca wood decay)
Grape with Esca (Black Measles).treatment: There is no cure for Esca once established. Prune out infected wood aggressively. Paint wounds with wound protectant immediately after pruning. Remove and burn severely infected vines. Replant with certified disease-free stock.

symptoms: Angular, dark brown spots on upper leaf surfaces
White to gray powdery sporulation on the underside of spots
Infected leaves may turn yellow and drop prematurely
Grape with Isariopsis Leaf Spot.treatment: Apply copper-based or mancozeb fungicide. Improve air circulation by leaf pulling in the fruit zone. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which promotes dense canopy growth.

symptoms: No disease detected — your grape plant appears healthy!
Healthy Grape Plant.treatment: Maintain regular dormant pruning and train vines for airflow. Apply preventive fungicide program starting at bud break.

symptoms: Asymmetric yellowing of leaves (yellow dragon pattern)
Misshapen, bitter, and small fruit that remains partly green
Tree decline with twig dieback and sparse canopy
Orange with Citrus Greening.treatment: There is currently no cure for Citrus Greening (HLB). Control the Asian citrus psyllid (the insect vector) using systemic insecticides. Remove and destroy infected trees to prevent spread. Replant with certified disease-free, psyllid-free trees.

symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn dark and fall out (shot-hole appearance)
Fruit develops sunken, dark, cracked lesions
Severe defoliation in wet seasons
Peach with Bacterial Spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide starting at petal fall and repeat every 10–14 days. Plant resistant varieties. Avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen. Prune to open canopy and reduce leaf wetness duration.

symptoms: No disease detected — your peach plant appears healthy!
Healthy Peach Plant.treatment: Apply dormant copper spray before bud break. Maintain proper thinning to prevent overcrowding of fruit.

symptoms: Small, water-soaked, circular spots on leaves with yellow halos
Spots turn brown and necrotic; leaves drop prematurely
Fruit develops raised, dark, rough lesions
Bell Pepper with Bacterial Spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide preventively and after rain events. Use drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers. Plant certified disease-free seed or transplants. Remove and destroy infected plant debris.

symptoms: No disease detected — your bell pepper plant appears healthy!
Healthy Bell Pepper Plant.treatment: Water at the base of plants to minimize leaf wetness. Rotate crops each season to prevent soilborne disease buildup.

symptoms: Dark brown, circular spots with concentric rings (target-board pattern) on lower leaves
Yellow halo surrounds each spot
Infected leaves turn yellow and die from the bottom up
Potato with Early Blight.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin fungicide when the first lesions appear. Maintain adequate potassium fertilization (potassium deficiency increases susceptibility). Remove infected lower leaves. Rotate crops.

symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked, dark green to brown lesions on leaves
White mold visible on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Stems develop brown-black rot
Tubers develop reddish-brown dry rot
Potato with Late Blight.treatment: Apply metalaxyl + mancozeb or cymoxanil fungicide immediately. This disease spreads very rapidly — act within 24 hours of detection. Destroy infected plants (do not compost). This is the disease that caused the Irish Potato Famine.

symptoms: No disease detected — your potato plant appears healthy!
Healthy Potato Plant.treatment: Hill soil around stems as plants grow to protect developing tubers. Rotate with non-solanaceous crops each season.

symptoms: No disease detected — your raspberry plant appears healthy!
Healthy Raspberry Plant.treatment: Prune out all floricanes after harvest. Maintain good spacing for air circulation. Apply sulfur-based fungicide preventively at bud break.

symptoms: No disease detected — your soybean plant appears healthy!
Healthy Soybean Plant.treatment: Scout fields regularly. Maintain proper plant spacing. Rotate with non-leguminous crops.

symptoms: White, powdery fungal coating on upper and lower leaf surfaces
Affected leaves turn yellow and eventually brown
Reduced fruit production in severe cases
Squash with Powdery Mildew.treatment: Apply potassium bicarbonate, neem oil, or sulfur-based fungicide at first sign of disease. Ensure adequate plant spacing for air circulation. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which promotes soft, susceptible tissue.

symptoms: Small, dark purple or reddish-purple spots on upper leaf surface
Spots enlarge and centers turn tan or gray
Severely infected leaves have a scorched appearance
Strawberry with Leaf Scorch.treatment: Apply captan or myclobutanil fungicide. Remove infected older leaves (renovation mowing after harvest). Plant resistant varieties. Avoid overhead irrigation.

symptoms: No disease detected — your strawberry plant appears healthy!
Healthy Strawberry Plant.treatment: Renovate planting after harvest by mowing leaves. Apply straw mulch to reduce soil splash and fruit rot.

symptoms: Small, water-soaked, circular spots on leaves with yellow halos
Spots turn dark brown or black and may fall out, creating shot-hole appearance
Fruit develops raised, rough, dark spots
Tomato with Bacterial Spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide plus mancozeb. Use drip irrigation. Plant resistant varieties. Remove infected debris at end of season.

symptoms: Dark brown, circular spots with concentric rings (target-board pattern) on older, lower leaves
Yellow halo surrounds the spots
Infected leaves turn yellow and drop, starting from the bottom of the plant
Tomato with Early Blight.treatment: Remove infected lower leaves promptly. Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper-based fungicide every 7–10 days. Mulch around the base of plants to prevent soil splash. Stake or cage plants to improve airflow.

symptoms: Large, irregular, dark brown, greasy-looking lesions on leaves
White fuzzy mold on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Stems and fruit develop brown, firm rot
Tomato with Late Blight.treatment: Apply metalaxyl or cymoxanil-based fungicide immediately — Late Blight spreads extremely fast. Remove and bag infected plant material (do not compost). In severe cases, remove entire plants to prevent spread to neighbors.

symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces
Velvety olive-green to grayish-brown mold on the underside of leaves
Infected leaves curl, wither, and drop
Tomato with Leaf Mold.treatment: Improve greenhouse ventilation or plant spacing to reduce humidity. Apply copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicide. Remove infected leaves. Water in the morning so foliage dries before evening.

symptoms: Many small, circular spots with dark brown borders and tan/gray centers
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) visible inside spots with a magnifying glass
Rapid defoliation starting from the bottom of the plant
Tomato with Septoria Leaf Spot.treatment: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves immediately. Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper fungicide every 7–10 days. Avoid wetting foliage when watering. Rotate crops and remove all plant debris at season end.

symptoms: Fine webbing on the underside of leaves
Leaves show yellow stippling or bronze discoloration
Severe infestations cause leaves to dry out and drop
Tomato with Spider Mites or Two-spotted.treatment: Spider mites are not fungi — they are tiny arachnids. Spray plants with a strong stream of water to knock mites off. Apply neem oil, insecticidal soap, or miticide (e.g. bifenazate). Introduce predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) as a biological control.

symptoms: Circular brown spots with concentric rings on leaves, stems, and fruit
Spots may coalesce causing large dead areas
Fruit shows sunken, dark, circular lesions
Tomato with Target Spot.treatment: Apply azoxystrobin or chlorothalonil fungicide. Remove infected plant parts. Ensure adequate plant spacing and staking. Avoid working in wet plants to prevent spreading spores.

symptoms: Leaves curl upward and inward with yellowing margins
Stunted plant growth with small, chlorotic leaves
Severe flower drop and very low fruit set
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.treatment: There is no cure for TYLCV once a plant is infected. Control the whitefly vector with insecticides (imidacloprid) or reflective mulch. Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Plant resistant varieties (labeled TYLCV-resistant).

symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green on leaves (mottling)
Leaves may be distorted, blistered, or fern-like
Fruit may show uneven ripening or yellow patches
Tomato Mosaic Virus.treatment: There is no cure for Tomato Mosaic Virus. Remove and destroy infected plants. Wash hands and tools with soap and water before handling plants (the virus spreads by contact). Plant resistant varieties. Control aphid vectors.

symptoms: No disease detected — your tomato plant appears healthy!
Healthy Tomato Plant.treatment: Stake or cage plants for support. Apply balanced fertilizer and water consistently to prevent blossom end rot. Scout weekly for early pest and disease signs.
